claude.country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)
claude.sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment

links.outcome: Readability of original guideline-based patient education materials versus GPT-4 generated versions
links.effect: Original PEMs had higher reading levels than GPT-4 PEMs (FKGL 11.6 vs 6.1, p<.001); FKRE 43.5 vs 70.8, p<.001.
links.quote: The required reading education levels were higher for original PEMs compared to GPT-4 generated PEMs (Mean FKGL: 11.6 vs. 6.1; p < .001).

links.outcome: Reading level of original patient materials versus appropriate level
links.effect: Original EAU PEMs required higher reading grade level (FKGL 11.6, GFS 14.3) than GPT-4 PEMs (FKGL 6.1, GFS 7.4); the original PEMs did not meet EU readability standards.
links.quote: Moreover, it has been noted that certain sections of PEMs exhibit poor readability, not meeting the readability standards set by the European Union (EU) for patient facing material [ 8 ].

links.outcome: Accuracy, completeness, clarity of GPT-4 PEMs versus original PEMs rated by expert urologists
links.effect: No significant differences for localized or metastatic disease; correctness trifecta reached in 92/160 original vs 81/160 GPT-4 PEMs (p=.217).
links.quote: The correctness trifecta was reached in 92/160 rated original PEM and 81/160 rated GPT-4 generated PEM (p = .217).

links.outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4 PEMs grounded in EAU guidelines versus original PEMs
links.effect: Guideline-grounded GPT-4 PEMs were not significantly different from original PEMs in accuracy (e.g., prostate localized 4.3 vs 3.7, p=.122); no comparison against ungrounded GPT-4.
links.quote: For localized disease, the original PEM was not significantly different from the GPT-4 generated PEM for mean (SD) accuracy [prostate cancer: 4.3 (0.7) vs 3.7 (1.1), p = .122;

links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of unedited GPT-4 PEMs that would need review before release
links.effect: Unedited GPT-4 PEMs were rated similar to original PEMs, but agreement on all three correctness metrics was reached in only 81/160 ratings; authors say human oversight is still required.
links.quote: Neither original PEMs nor GPT-4 generated PEMs are flawless, despite an overall agreement on correctness of the information by the expert raters in our study.

links.outcome: Faithfulness and clarity of GPT-4 translations of PEMs into five EU languages rated by native speakers
links.effect: Translated PEMs rated faithful in 62/80 (77.5%) and clear in 54/80 (67.5%) cases.
links.quote: Translated PEMs were rated as faithful in 62/80 (77.5%) cases and clear in 54/80 (67.5%) cases for the different languages assessed.

unlisted_practices: Using clinical guidelines as knowledge base for LLM-generated patient education materials
Using LLMs to simplify patient materials to a target readability level
Availability of original patient materials in multiple languages

links.effect: GPT-4 PEMs had lower reading grade levels than originals: FKGL 6.1 vs 11.6; GFS 7.4 vs 14.3; SI 6.3 vs 10.6; all p < .001.
links.quote: In line, the required reading education levels were higher (less readable) for original PEMs [FKGL: 11.6 (2.4); GFS: 14.3 (2.5); SI: 10.6 (1.8); CLI: 14.2 (1.5); ARI: 11.6 (3.0)] compared to GPT4-generated PEMs [FKGL: 6.1 (0.9), p < .001; GFS: 7.4 (0.8), p < .001; SI: 6.3 (0.6), p < .001; CLI: 11.7 (1.3), p = .004; ARI: 6.1 (1.3), p < .001, see Fig 2 ].

links.effect: GPT-4 PEMs had FKRE 70.8 vs 43.5 for originals (p < .001) and correctness trifecta 81/160 vs 92/160 (p = .217).
links.quote: The readability scores for original PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 43.5 (10.8)] were lower than for GPT-4 generated PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 70.8 (4.9), p < .001].

links.effect: Guideline-based GPT-4 PEMs were not significantly different in accuracy/completeness/clarity; correctness trifecta reached 81/160 GPT-4 vs 92/160 original ratings (p = .217).
links.quote: The correctness trifecta was reached in 92/160 rated original PEM and 81/160 rated GPT-4 generated PEM (p = .217).

links.effect: Correctness trifecta reached 81/160 GPT-4 ratings; authors state neither original nor GPT-4 PEMs were flawless.
links.quote: Neither original PEMs nor GPT-4 generated PEMs are flawless, despite an overall agreement on correctness of the information by the expert raters in our study.

unlisted_practices: AI translation of patient education materials into multiple languages assessed for faithfulness and clarity

links.effect: Mean Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease was 70.8 for GPT-4 generated PEMs versus 43.5 for original PEMs (p < .001), indicating significantly better readability.
links.quote: The readability scores for original PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 43.5 (10.8)] were lower than for GPT-4 generated PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 70.8 (4.9), p < .001].
